metadata.title: TIMSS & PIRLS Lynch School of Education International Study Center SUPPLEMENT 3: VARIABLES DERIVED FROM THE STUDENT, HOME, TEACHER, AND SCHOOL QUESTIONNAIRE DATA — PIRLS 2016 USER GUIDE FOR THE INTERNATIONAL DATABASE
metadata.venue: IEA (International Association for the Evaluation of Educational Achievement)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS 2016 International Database user guide supplement describing how derived questionnaire variables are computed (e.g., recodes and composite indices) for use in PIRLS 2016 international reporting exhibits. It does not provide an analysis sample, estimation model, or instructions for applying complex survey weights to student achievement outcomes. For users conducting analyses with PIRLS 2016 microdata, weighting and replicate-weight procedures should follow the main PIRLS 2016 user guide / technical documentation for the international database (not included in this supplement). The derived variables here specify missing-data rules for the source questionnaire items (e.g., setting derived variables to missing when any required source variable is missing), but they do not specify weight variables or replicate design methods.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this supplement does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes or provide PV-based modeling; it only documents how questionnaire-derived background variables are constructed for reporting. Missing-data handling is also not reported in the sense of an estimation strategy (e.g., listwise deletion or imputation) because the supplement specifies deterministic missing rules for derived variables (set to missing when source variables are missing) rather than an analytic missing-data method. Therefore, the appropriate interpretation is that PVs and analytic missing-data handling are outside the scope of this documentation-only supplement.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used for documentation of derived variables in the PIRLS 2016 International Database; no analytic sample or country-specific student counts are provided in this supplement.

data.outcome_summary: This supplement is not an empirical study; it is a PIRLS 2016 International Database user guide supplement that documents how derived background variables are computed from the Student, Home, Teacher, and School questionnaires. It provides, for each derived variable, the derived variable name/label, the international report exhibit(s) where it is reported, and the exact computation procedure including source questionnaire items and deterministic missing-data rules (e.g., set the derived variable to missing if any required source variable is missing). The examples shown include composites such as home study supports/digital supports, parents’ highest education and occupation recodes, and school instructional time and library/computer availability indicators. Because no predictive modeling, sampling, scaling, or PV-based achievement analysis is conducted here, there are no performance metrics or causal/predictive effects to interpret for policy; instead, the practical implication is correct variable construction and consistent missing rules for downstream PIRLS 2016 analyses and reporting.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a documentation supplement (variable derivation guide) rather than an empirical ML/predictive paper or an IEA/OECD technical report with reported model results. As a result, fields such as total_students, countries, PV handling, missing-data handling strategy for estimation, and ML techniques are not applicable or not reported because the document does not run analyses on a student sample. The extraction therefore focuses on the methodological content of variable construction and missing rules, not on study outcomes.
